description:
crate-jmap-types/src/resultref.rs:73 contains:

    /// The resolver in kith-jmap evaluates Ref variants before method dispatch.

`kith-jmap` is a workspace-internal / Mark-private repository name
(per workspace AGENTS.md, the kith family lives at ~/PROJECT/kith).
This doc-comment is published on docs.rs as part of `jmap-types`'s
rustdoc. An external reader sees \"kith-jmap\" and cannot resolve it.

What a caller depending on this API in production accepts:

1. The rustdoc on `Argument<T>` is the canonical place for callers to
   learn how Ref dispatch works. Following the prose chases a dead
   reference (kith-jmap is not a published crate, not a public repo,
   not a documented project).
2. The actual dispatcher implementation lives in `jmap-server` in this
   workspace. That is the public, on-crates.io reference the reader
   should see. The original kith-jmap was the source from which
   jmap-server was extracted (per workspace AGENTS.md \"Source
   Material\" table); the comment was carried over without updating.

Fix candidates:
- Change \"kith-jmap\" to \"jmap-server\" (or to \"the dispatcher in
  jmap-server\"). One-line edit.
- Or: drop the implementation reference entirely. The doc-comment
  explains *what* `Ref` means (dispatch-time substitution); naming
  *who* substitutes is implementation detail that doesn't belong on
  the wire type's rustdoc.

Grep result: this is the only `kith` reference left in the
crate-jmap-types/src tree. AGENTS.md still references kith correctly
as a source-material repo for contributors, which is appropriate
(internal contributor guidance); the rustdoc is the external surface
and should be cleaned.
title: Argument<T> rustdoc references private repo 'kith-jmap' on public docs.rs surface
